 For the past couple of years, it feels like every few months I get an email saying the monthly subscription fee for one of the streaming services I pay for is going up. Just this year alone, Netflix, Disney+, HBO Max, Apple TV, Paramount+, and more have all raised their prices, making streaming even more expensive than it already was. But there has been one silver lining in all this. While streaming costs have sharply risen recently, free streaming alternatives have only gotten better.

 There are so many great free streaming services to choose from nowadays, including Pluto TV, Tubi, JustWatch TV, Plex, and The Roku Channel. And while there is sometimes a misconception that free streaming services don't have as much to offer as paid services, that certainly isn't the case. Just look at The Roku Channel . It's always been one of my favorites, and it offers a huge selection of over 80,000 on-demand movies and shows you can stream anytime for free, plus one of the largest lineups of free live TV channels, with more than 500 available. 
 And just like paid streaming services, which are always adding new content, free streaming services are as well, and The Roku Channel is no exception. Roku has been on a roll, adding new free content every month this year, especially live TV channels. This November, it's keeping its streak going by adding eight more free channels to its lineup.

 Which free channels have joined The Roku Channel?
 Roku's free channel lineup continues to expand
 Earlier this month, Roku added five new free channels to its lineup, but just ahead of Thanksgiving, it's back at it again with another wave, this time adding eight new channels, according to Cord Cutter News . 
 Highlights from this latest wave of free channels include Swerve Sports Talk , which airs popular sports podcasts covering a wide range of sports, including the NFL, NBA, MLB, Formula 1, and college football and college basketball; Roku Case of the Week , which focuses on true-crime and investigative series; Botherd , which broadcasts conversational and comedy-focused talk series; and finally Ideas en 5 Minutos , a Spanish-language lifestyle and how-to channel.
 You can check out all 8 of the new free channels Roku added below, along with their channel numbers:
 Swerve Sports Talk (#814)
 365 BLK (#2417)
 Roku Case of the Week (#2516)
 Snapped (#2688)
 Botherd (#4523)
 1230! Spanish (#5120)
 Ideas en 5 Minutos (#5121)
 Zona (#5122)
 Quiz 8 Questions · Test Your Knowledge Roku streaming devices
Trivia challenge
 From its humble beginnings to your living room — how well do you really know Roku?
 History Hardware Features Streaming Founders Begin 01 / 8 History In what year was Roku founded?
 A 2005 B 2008 C 2002 D 2010 Correct! Roku was founded in 2008 by Anthony Wood, who had previously founded ReplayTV. The company launched its first streaming player the same year it was founded, making it a pivotal moment in streaming history. Not quite. Roku was founded in 2008 by Anthony Wood. It launched its very first streaming device that same year, just months after the company was formed, which was remarkably fast for a hardware startup. Continue 02 / 8 Founders Who is the founder and CEO of Roku?
 A Reed Hastings B Andy Jassy C Anthony Wood D Tony Fadell Correct! Anthony Wood founded Roku in 2008 and has served as its CEO ever since. Before Roku, he founded ReplayTV, one of the first digital video recorder companies, giving him deep roots in home entertainment technology. Not quite. The answer is Anthony Wood. He founded Roku in 2008 after previously founding ReplayTV. Reed Hastings is associated with Netflix, while Tony Fadell is known as a key figure behind the iPod and Nest. Continue 03 / 8 History Roku was originally spun off from which major streaming company?
 A Hulu B Amazon C Netflix D HBO Correct! Roku started as an internal project at Netflix, which invested in the company and helped shape its early direction. Netflix ultimately decided to spin it off as a separate company to avoid competing with other device manufacturers who might not want to carry a Netflix-branded box. Not quite. Roku was actually spun off from Netflix. Netflix funded and incubated the project before deciding it was better to keep the streaming device market open and neutral rather than launch a Netflix-branded player that might alienate other hardware partners. Continue 04 / 8 Hardware What was the name of Roku's very first streaming device, launched in 2008?
 A Roku HD Player B Roku DVP N1000 C Roku Streaming Stick D Roku XR Correct! The Roku DVP N1000, also known as the Roku Digital Video Player, was the company's debut product. It launched in May 2008 at a price of $99 and could stream Netflix content directly to your TV — a genuinely groundbreaking feature at the time. Not quite. The first Roku device was the Roku DVP N1000, launched in May 2008. Priced at $99, it was primarily designed to stream Netflix and helped pioneer the idea of a dedicated, affordable streaming box for the living room. Continue 05 / 8 Features What is the name of Roku's free, ad-supported streaming channel built directly into its platform?
 A Roku Now B Roku Freeview C The Roku Channel D Roku Live Correct! The Roku Channel launched in 2017 and offers thousands of free, ad-supported movies and TV shows. It has since become one of the most-watched channels on the Roku platform and is also available on other devices and the web. Not quite. The correct answer is The Roku Channel, which launched in 2017. It provides free, ad-supported content and has grown into a major part of Roku's business strategy, helping the company earn revenue beyond just hardware sales. Continue 06 / 8 Streaming Roku's business model relies heavily on which of the following revenue streams?
 A Monthly subscription fees from users B Platform advertising and content partnerships C Selling user data to third parties D Hardware sales only Correct! While Roku does sell hardware, its primary revenue engine is its platform business, which includes advertising, revenue sharing with streaming partners, and The Roku Channel. This platform-first approach is what makes Roku more than just a device maker. Not quite. Roku makes the majority of its money from its platform business, which includes advertising and revenue-sharing arrangements with streaming services. Hardware sales are actually sold at low margins, with the real profit coming from keeping users engaged on the platform. Continue 07 / 8 Hardware Which of the following form factors did Roku introduce to make streaming even more portable and discreet?
 A A Blu-ray add-on module B A plug-in HDMI streaming stick C A router with built-in streaming D A soundbar with integrated apps Correct! Roku introduced the Roku Streaming Stick, a compact dongle that plugs directly into a TV's HDMI port. It was a game-changer for portability, making it easy to turn any modern TV into a smart TV without a bulky box sitting on your shelf. Not quite. Roku launched the Roku Streaming Stick, a small dongle that plugs straight into an HDMI port. This compact form factor made Roku devices far more discreet and portable, competing directly with Amazon's Fire TV Stick. Continue 08 / 8 History In which year did Roku go public on the Nasdaq stock exchange?
 A 2015 B 2019 C 2017 D 2021 Correct! Roku went public on September 28, 2017, trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ROKU. Its IPO was considered a major success, and the stock surged significantly in the months that followed, reflecting strong investor confidence in the streaming market. Not quite. Roku held its IPO on September 28, 2017, listing on the Nasdaq under the ticker ROKU. The offering was well-received by investors and marked a major milestone in the company's journey from a Netflix spin-off to a publicly traded streaming powerhouse.  Where to find these free channels and more on Roku
 You can easily search by name or channel number
 If you want to dive into any of the new free channels Roku has added, you'll find them in the Live TV Guide within The Roku Channel app. The experience is similar to a cable TV guide. When you open Roku's Live TV Guide, you'll see a full list of the channels it offers, along with a list of categories on the left side of the guide that help you quickly browse by genre, like News, Sports, Entertainment, Classic TV, Music, Comedy, and more.
 To quickly find any of the new channels Roku just added, you can search by channel number to jump right to it by pressing the Star (*) button on your remote, then selecting the "Jump to channel" option that appears on the screen. Then enter the channel number, and it will start playing.
 The Roku Channel app is available on all Roku smart TVs and streaming devices, as well as Google TV and Fire TV devices. You can also download the Roku app on iOS and Android, or watch The Roku Channel directly through its website.
 Additionally, if you're looking to search across all the free channels Roku offers, it has a search function on the left side of its Live TV Guide that you can use to find any channel by name, or to search for specific topics like cars or action movies.
 With over 80,000 on-demand movies and TV shows and over 500 free live TV channels, The Roku Channel continues to grow, and this latest wave of free channels is yet another example. But beyond The Roku Channel, if you're looking for even more free content to stream, I recommend exploring Plex, Pluto TV, and Tubi.
